newsitem.title: CHINA: China's trains to run faster from April.
newsitem.headline: China's trains to run faster from April.

text.p: China's lumbering trains that can take days to chug between cities will be speeded up from April to try to lure back passengers, the Xinhua news agency said on Monday.
Major inter-city rail journeys would be quicker from April when train speeds were increased to more than 110 kph (66 mph), it said. It did not give the current speed of China's trains.
The faster trains would run on long-distance journeys of 1,000-1,500 km (600-900 miles) starting from such major cities as Beijing and Shanghai, it said.
By the end of the century, China would take delivery of 64 "arrive-in-a-night" long-distance passenger trains, it quoted Zhou Yimin, deputy chief engineer of the Ministry of Railways, as saying.
Poor marketing and service coupled with the slow speed of China's trains have contributed to a drop in passenger transport in recent years as more affluent travellers choose to travel by air or car.
China's trains carried 942 million travellers last year, a drop of 12.3 percent compared with 1995.
The speed of freight trains would also be raised to about 80 kph (48 mph) from about 60 kph (36 mph), Zhou said.
